Kingma & Welling, "Auto-Encoding Variational Bayes" (2013) · Higgins et al., "β-VAE: Learning Basic Visual Concepts with a Constrained Variational Framework" (2017)

β-VAE on MNIST

Re-implemented · original code

What I built

A convolutional VAE on MNIST in PyTorch. The loss is a Bernoulli reconstruction term (binary cross entropy) plus β times the KL divergence, and β is a command-line flag. The pretrained checkpoint uses a 20-dimensional latent space; the training script defaults to 10.

Around the model I wrote tools for looking at the latent space: linear and spherical (SLERP) interpolation between two digits, a t-SNE map of the 10,000 test digits, and a Streamlit app that ties them together.

Results Qualitative only so far. The one observation in the repo is that β = 0.5 gives clear clusters. I have not run a quantitative evaluation, so there are no metrics here.

Faithful vs changed

Which parts of the papers the code keeps and which it changes
PartStatusIn the code
EncoderFaithfulGaussian posterior with the reparameterization trick.
Decoder likelihoodFaithfulBernoulli, trained with binary cross entropy.
ObjectiveFaithfulβ-weighted KL term against the standard normal prior.
DatasetSimplifiedMNIST only.
β scheduleSimplifiedFixed β per run, no annealing schedule.
ArchitectureChangedConvolutional layers of my own choosing, not copied from a paper.
